mainTopic: When can the offspring of a holy animal itself be offered according to רבי אלעזר? The גמרא gives רבא's and אביי's explanations, with challenges from two ברייתות about a female set aside for a פסח.
overview: The גמרא finishes רבא's explanation of רבי אלעזר: an offspring itself can be offered only when its mother carried that same status. So the offspring of a תמורת אשם is not offered as an עולה; only its money buys one. אביי objects with a ברייתא. In it, a female set aside for a פסח gives birth after פסח, and רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is offered as שלמים, even though the mother was a פסח. רבא answers that after פסח a leftover פסח becomes שלמים, so the mother did have that status. He also agrees that רבי אלעזר would argue before פסח too. אביי gives his own explanation instead. There is a tradition that the offspring goes wherever the leftover (מותר) goes, so after פסח it is שלמים, but before פסח it is only for the money of a פסח, like its mother. רב עוקבא בר חמא challenges אביי from a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is offered as a פסח. רבינא answers that the case is an animal that was already pregnant when set aside, and a fetus is a separate animal (רבי יוחנן), so it became holy directly. מר זוטרא supports this from the ברייתא's words 'it and its offspring.'

steps.title: Where the mother has no עולה status, only the money is used
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his explanation. With the offspring of a תמורת אשם, רבי אלעזר agrees that the animal itself is not offered as an עולה. Only an animal bought with its money is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering, whose mother never had the status of a burnt offering, רבי אלעזר agrees: its money, yes, can buy a burnt offering, but the animal itself is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation of when רבי אלעזר lets an offspring itself be brought as a קרבן. Here it gives the case where he agrees that it cannot be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the offspring itself can be offered as an עולה only if its mother already had the name 'עולה' on her. In the case of a תמורת אשם, the mother's status came from an אשם, not an עולה. So the offspring itself cannot go up on the מזבח, and only its sale money is used for an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal someone tried to swap in place of a קרבן. It becomes holy too.
Offspring, the baby of a holy animal.
Guilt offering.
The label or status of a burnt offering.
With its money, meaning the money received when it is sold.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule אביי will test: רבי אלעזר allows the offspring itself to be offered only when the mother carried that same status.

phrases.english: But regarding the offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering,
where there is no burnt-offering status on its mother,
Rabbi Elazar concedes
that with its money, yes, a burnt offering is brought,
but it itself is not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and finishes רבא's explanation of רבי אלעזר from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without עולה status on the mother, the offspring itself is not offered; only its money buys an עולה.

steps.title: אביי asks whether רבי אלעזר really needs the mother's status
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the idea that רבי אלעזר needs the mother to carry the status. He begins quoting a ברייתא about a female set aside for a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Does רבי אלעזר really require the mother to have burnt-offering status? But a ברייתא teaches: If someone sets aside a female for his פסח, it grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and he buys a פסח with the money. If it gave birth, the offspring grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and he buys a פסח with its money.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation and starts bringing a ברייתא as his source. This part of the ברייתא is setup; the key line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח must be a male, so a female set aside for it cannot be brought, and neither can her offspring. Both are left to graze until they get a blemish, and their money buys a proper פסח. This sets the scene for what happens after פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A female animal.
The Paschal offering, which must be a male.
It grazes, meaning it is left out to pasture.
Until it becomes unfit, usually by getting a blemish, so it can be sold.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
And does Rabbi Elazar require
burnt-offering status on its mother?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
One who designates a female for his Paschal offering,
it grazes until it becomes unfit,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; read the word in square brackets instead, which is the feminine form.

phrases.english: and it is sold, and he brings a Paschal offering with its money.
If it gave birth,
it grazes until it becomes unfit,
and it is sold, and he brings a Paschal offering with its money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְכִי בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the requirement stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי אלעזר requires the mother to carry the same status.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא will show רבי אלעזר letting an offspring itself be offered even though the mother lacked that status.

steps.title: After פסח, רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with the case after פסח. The תנא קמא says to sell the animals and buy שלמים, but רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is offered as שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal was still unblemished after פסח, it grazes until it gets a blemish, and he buys שלמים with its money. If it gave birth, the offspring grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and he buys שלמים with its money. רבי אלעזר says: the offspring itself is offered as שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of אביי's proof. רבי אלעזר lets the offspring itself be brought as שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother was set aside as a פסח, not as שלמים. Even so, רבי אלעזר allows her offspring to be offered directly as שלמים. That seems to contradict the rule from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: It was left over, meaning it stayed unused and unblemished.
Peace offering.
It itself is offered, instead of only its money being used.

phrases.english: If it remained until after Passover,
it grazes until it becomes unfit,
and he brings a peace offering with its money.
If it gave birth, it grazes until it becomes unfit,
and it is sold, and he brings a peace offering with its money.
Rabbi Elazar says:
It itself is sacrificed as a peace offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא אביי began quoting.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר does not require the mother to carry the offspring's status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a female designated as a פסח that gave birth after פסח.

steps.title: אביי spells out the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the mother never had שלמים status, yet רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is offered as שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here the mother does not have peace-offering status, and still רבי אלעזר says the offspring is offered as a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains exactly why the ברייתא is a problem for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said רבי אלעזר allows the offspring itself only when the mother had the same status. Here the mother was a פסח, not שלמים, and yet the offspring itself is brought as שלמים. So, אביי argues, the mother's status should not matter to רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here: points to a case that contradicts the claim.
The label or status of a peace offering.

phrases.english: But here,
where there is no peace-offering status on its mother,
yet Rabbi Elazar says it is sacrificed as a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלֵיכָּא שֵׁם שְׁלָמִים עַל אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in step 3 against step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 1 that the mother must carry the status.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mother was a פסח with no שלמים status, yet her offspring is offered directly as שלמים.

steps.title: After פסח, a leftover פסח is already שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that after פסח is a special case. A leftover פסח is itself offered as שלמים, so the mother really did have שלמים status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You are bringing a case of 'after פסח'? After פסח is different, because a leftover פסח is itself offered as a peace offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his explanation by showing that אביי's case actually fits his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once פסח has passed, a leftover פסח animal automatically becomes שלמים. So the mother here did have שלמים status after פסח. That is why רבי אלעזר lets her offspring itself be offered as שלמים, and רבא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different.
A leftover פסח: an animal set aside for the פסח but not used. It is brought as שלמים.
Itself, the animal's own body.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי אלעזר lets the offspring itself be offered only when the mother carries that status. After פסח the mother counts as שלמים, because a leftover פסח becomes שלמים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say the mother lacks the category of a קרבן. His point is that after פסח the mother's פסח status turns into שלמים status, so the case fits his rule.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the name in round brackets; read the name in square brackets instead: it's רבא answering אביי.

phrases.english: Are you saying a case of 'after Passover'?
After Passover is different,
since a leftover Paschal offering itself is sacrificed as a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא אַחַר הַפֶּסַח קָא אָמְרַתְּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the challenging case actually meets the requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the mother, set aside as a פסח, had no שלמים status.
steps.terutzMaskana: After פסח, a leftover פסח becomes שלמים, so the mother did have שלמים status and רבא's rule holds.

steps.title: Then רבי אלעזר should argue in the first case too
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that if רבא's reasoning is right, רבי אלעזר should also argue in the case where the animal gave birth before פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let רבי אלעזר also argue in the first part of the ברייתא!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's answer from step 5. He says רבא's logic should also apply to the first case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the mother had שלמים status, so the offspring can be offered itself. But a פסח brought before פסח as a שלמים is also valid, so the mother has that status before פסח too. So why does רבי אלעזר only argue in the case after פסח?

keyTerms.meaning: The first part (first case) of a ברייתא or משנה
If so: introduces a challenge that follows from what was just said

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the reason is that the mother has שלמים status, like רבא said in step 5.

phrases.english: let him also disagree in the first clause!
phrases.notes: The first clause is the ברייתא's case where the animal gave birth before פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far רבא's answer in step 5 reaches
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the mother's שלמים status allows the offspring to be offered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same status exists before פסח, yet the ברייתא shows רבי אלעזר arguing only about the case after פסח

steps.title: רבא agrees: they argue in the first case too
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts the point and says that רבי אלעזר really does argue in the first case as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Yes, that is true, and they do argue there too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not fight the challenge. He agrees that רבי אלעזר argues before פסח too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer is a full agreement. The ברייתא only spells out the argument in one case, but by רבא's logic רבי אלעזר would also let the offspring born before פסח be offered as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so: agreeing with the questioner's point
They disagree

phrases.english: He said to him:
Yes, it is indeed so, and they disagree.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אלעזר and the תנא קמא argue in the before-פסח case too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, וּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by agreeing with it
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the argument applies there too
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר only argues about the offspring after פסח
steps.terutzMaskana: By רבא's view, רבי אלעזר argues in both cases

steps.title: אביי's own explanation: the offspring follows the leftover
steps.stepSummary: אביי says nobody argues about the case before פסח. There is a tradition that the offspring goes where the leftover פסח goes, and after פסח a leftover is offered as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Nobody argues at all about the first case. We have a tradition that wherever the leftover goes, the offspring goes. After פסח, a leftover is offered as a שלמים, so the offspring is also offered as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different way to understand רבי אלעזר. It is based on a tradition about the offspring following the מותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the mother's status was the key. For אביי, the key is a received rule: the offspring is treated like a leftover פסח. After פסח, a leftover becomes a שלמים, so the offspring itself can be a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (a received teaching)
Leftover: an animal set aside for a קרבן that ended up not being used for it
Offspring
Nobody disagrees at all

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second, different reason for רבי אלעזר. It limits the argument to after פסח, where רבא had said they argue in both cases.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
no one disagrees at all,
phrases.notes: He means in the first case, before פסח. There everyone agrees the offspring itself is not offered.

phrases.english: for it is learned as a tradition
to the place that the leftover goes, the offspring goes;
after Passover, when the leftover is offered as a peace offering,
the offspring is also offered as a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לָא פְּלִיג מִידֵּי, דִּגְמִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation from רבא's in steps 5 and 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring follows the status of a leftover פסח; after פסח that means שלמים

steps.title: Before פסח, the offspring is only for the money of a פסח
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes: before פסח, the mother was set aside only to be sold for a פסח, so the offspring is also only for the money of a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But before פסח, what was the mother set aside for? For the money of a פסח. So the offspring is also for the money of a פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the case before פסח is different. Before פסח, the offspring just copies the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female cannot be a פסח itself, so she is holy only for her value: she is sold and a פסח is bought with the money. Before פסח there is no leftover yet, so the offspring has the same status as its mother. It too is only for the money of a פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: For the money (value) of a פסח: sold so a פסח can be bought with the money
He made it holy (set it aside)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: after פסח the offspring follows the leftover and becomes a שלמים. Before פסח it follows the mother and is only for the money of a פסח, and everyone agrees.

phrases.english: But before Passover,
for what was its mother consecrated?
For the value of a Paschal offering,
so the offspring is also for the value of a Paschal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח, אִימֵּיהּ לְמַאי אַקְדְּשַׁהּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before פסח, the offspring has the mother's status: only for the money of a פסח

steps.title: Does the offspring really just copy the mother?
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא questions אביי's claim that the offspring is only for the money of a פסח because its mother is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא raised a difficulty: Do we really say that since the mother is only for her money, the offspring is also only for its money?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is raised against אביי's step 9. This line opens the challenge, and the next step brings the source behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed that before פסח the offspring has exactly the mother's status. רב עוקבא בר חמא is about to show a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר does not treat it that way.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really say? This questions an assumption

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Ḥama raises an objection:
And do we say
that since its mother is for the value,
the offspring is also for the value?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן מִדְּאִימֵּיהּ לִדְמֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that before פסח the offspring is only for the money of a פסח, like its mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא (next step) shows רבי אלעזר letting the offspring itself be offered as a פסח

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is a פסח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא: a female set aside for a פסח and her offspring graze until blemished and are sold for a פסח. רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is offered as a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: If someone sets aside a female for a פסח, she and her offspring graze until they get a blemish, are sold, and a פסח is bought with the money. רבי אלעזר says: the offspring itself is offered as a פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוקבא בר חמא brings the source for his challenge. In it, רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself can be a פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother here is only for her money, yet רבי אלעזר lets the offspring itself be a פסח. This is not a שלמים after פסח but a פסח itself. So the offspring does not simply copy the mother, which goes against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: They graze until they get a blemish (become unfit to be offered)
A female animal
It itself (here, the offspring)

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי אלעזר says the offspring is offered as a פסח, not as a שלמים like in the earlier ברייתא after פסח. That is why it challenges אביי's 'before פסח it is only for money'.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
One who sets aside a female as a Paschal offering,
it and its offspring graze until they become unfit,
and they are sold, and he brings a Paschal offering with their money.
Rabbi Elazar says:
It itself is offered as a Paschal offering.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the offspring, not the female mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the challenge in step 10
steps.raayaObject: Against אביי: the offspring does not just copy the mother's 'for money' status
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is offered as a פסח

steps.title: The offspring does not follow its mother in רבי אלעזר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is completed. In the ברייתא, the mother is holy only for her money, yet רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is offered as a פסח. This contradicts אביי's rule that the offspring follows the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, the mother is holy only for her money value, and still רבי אלעזר says the offspring itself is brought as a פסח. We do not give it the same status as its mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it started in Step 10. It uses the ברייתא from Step 11 to attack אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that before פסח, the offspring is only for the money of a פסח, because its mother is only for money. But in the ברייתא, the mother is a female, so she is only for money. Even so, רבי אלעזר says her offspring itself is offered as a פסח. So the offspring has a higher status than its mother, which goes against אביי's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: For its money value. The animal is not offered itself; it is sold and the money buys a פסח.
Is offered (on the מזבח).
We give it the same status as its mother.

phrases.english: But here, where its mother is only for its money value,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הוּא עַצְמוֹ קָרֵב פֶּסַח,
phrases.english: and רבי אלעזר said: it (the offspring) itself is offered as a פסח,
and we do not give it the same status as its mother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא quoted in Step 11 directly against אביי's statement in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the offspring is only for the money of a פסח because its mother is only for money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי אלעזר has a mother that is only for money and an offspring that is offered itself. So the offspring's status does not depend on the mother's.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about an animal that was already pregnant
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the ברייתא is talking about someone who set aside a pregnant animal. Following רבי יוחנן, a fetus is a separate animal, so the fetus itself became holy as a פסח even though its mother could not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We are talking about someone who set aside a pregnant animal. רבי אלעזר holds like רבי יוחנן, who said that if someone leaves the fetus out, it is left out, because a fetus is not part of its mother's body. So it is only the mother that did not get the holiness of the animal itself. But the fetus did become holy as a פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends אביי. He explains that רבי אלעזר's case is different, because the fetus was already there when the animal was set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that a fetus counts as its own animal, not a body part of its mother. So when the pregnant female was set aside for a פסח, the fetus could become holy as a פסח in its own right. Only the mother failed to, because she is female. The offspring is offered because it was set aside directly, not because it follows its mother, so אביי's rule about offspring conceived later still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant animal.
If he left it out, it is left out. The owner can give the fetus a status separate from its mother's.
"A fetus is the thigh of its mother." This is the idea that a fetus is just a body part of the mother, which רבי יוחנן rejects here.
Holiness of the animal itself, so the animal itself is brought as a קרבן, not just its money.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying an offspring can have a higher status than its mother in general. It only works here because the fetus was already there when the animal was set aside, so the fetus itself became holy directly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps אביי's rule alive. Offspring conceived after the animal was set aside still follow the mother and are only for money.

phrases.english: רבינא said:
We are dealing with one who sets aside a pregnant animal,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר holds like רבי יוחנן, who said:
if he left it out, it is left out,
phrases.notes: He means that if the owner excludes the fetus from the mother's status, the fetus really is excluded.

phrases.english: because a fetus is not the thigh of its mother,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִמּוֹ הִיא דְּלָא קָדְשָׁה קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף,
phrases.english: and it is only its mother that did not become holy with the holiness of the animal itself,
but it did become holy.
phrases.notes: "It" here is the fetus, which became holy as a real פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: בְּמַפְרִישׁ בְּהֵמָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about an animal that was pregnant when it was set aside, together with the idea that a fetus is a separate animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The offspring in the ברייתא was conceived later, so רבי אלעזר is giving it a higher status than its mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fetus was already there when the animal was set aside and became holy as a פסח directly. אביי's rule for later offspring is untouched.

steps.title: The words "it and its offspring" show the animal was pregnant
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בריה דרב מרי supports רבינא. The ברייתא says "it and its offspring," which suggests the offspring already existed when the animal was set aside. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, the son of רב מרי, said to רבינא: It also makes sense that we are dealing with a pregnant animal, since the ברייתא says "it and its offspring." Learn from this that this is right.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא brings support for רבינא's answer from the wording of the ברייתא itself. The גמרא then agrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the mother and her offspring together, as if both were part of the original setting aside. That fits best if the offspring was already inside the mother at that moment. So רבינא's reading is not forced; the ברייתא's own words point to it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it stands to reason.
Her offspring.
Learn from this. The גמרא accepts the proof.

steps.whatToRemember: Offspring conceived after the animal was set aside follow their mother (אביי). A fetus that was already there when the animal was set aside can become holy on its own, as רבי אלעזר says, because a fetus is not part of its mother (רבי יוחנן).

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: מר זוטרא, the son of רב מרי, said to רבינא:
It also makes sense
that we are dealing with a pregnant animal,
since it teaches: "it and its offspring,"
phrases.notes: These are the words of the ברייתא from Step 11.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's answer in Step 13 from the ברייתא's own wording.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that the ברייתא is about an animal that was pregnant when it was set aside.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's phrase "היא וולדותיה" (it and its offspring), which treats the mother and offspring as set aside together.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is about a pregnant animal, so it does not contradict אביי.
